extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification. It contains 31,500 images across 45 scene classes, with substantial variation in translation, spatial resolution, viewpoint, object pose, illumination, background, and occlusion.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, and Xiaoqiang Lu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by selecting 45 scene classes from existing datasets and by searching relevant keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar; the images were then extracted by experts from Google Earth.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Remote sensing images from Google Earth, covering more than 100 countries and regions worldwide.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset was extracted by experts in remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth; the paper does not describe a human labeling task, instructions, workforce, or QC process.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is intentionally constructed to include high within-class diversity and between-class similarity, and it includes images from more than 100 countries and regions across developing, transition, and highly developed economies. The paper also notes that some classes have high semantic overlap (e.g., circular farmland vs. rectangular farmland, commercial area vs. industrial area), which may introduce class ambiguity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that existing remote sensing datasets suffer from small scale, limited class counts, limited image counts, lack of scene variation/diversity, and saturation of classification accuracy; the proposed dataset is designed to address these issues. It also notes that some classes have lower spatial resolutions than others. No explicit non-recommended uses are given.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented as a freely and publicly available benchmark intended to enable the community to develop and evaluate new data-driven algorithms for remote sensing scene classification, thereby supporting future research in intelligent earth observation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for remote sensing image scene classification, especially for training and evaluating data-driven algorithms and deep learning methods. The paper reports results as a baseline for future research.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Color histograms are computed in RGB color space and normalized to have an L1 norm of one; BoVW uses patch extraction by sampling local areas of images in a dense or sparse manner, feature descriptors are extracted, and codebooks are generated by unsupervised k-means clustering.
